text.p: Italian bonds and futures ended slightly firmer mainly in line with German bunds but in a market lacking fresh ideas and any real direction.
Operators said they were looking to U.S. producer price data out Thursday and paprticularly non-farm payrolls on Friday to provide impetus.
The March Btp future tested resistance at 128.00, touching a high of 128.15 but remained in a narrow range with a session low at 127.75. It closed 31 basis points up at 128.04.
Final Italian December CPI came in at 2.6 percent year-on-year as expected and provided little early inspiration.
The pay dispute between Italian metalworkers and employers is grinding on with no sign of an early solution, traders said, putting off hopes of an early Bank of Italy interest rate cut.
Italian President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro met central bank governor Antonio Fazio today but no further details were given.
"The market is having trouble sustaining rises, there is just no real impetus, one Milan trader said. In late APT trading in London the March Btp reached 128.20 before slipping back.
The Bundesbank is not expected to move on rates when it meets on Thursday. The spread over 10-year Bunds narrowed a touch to 169 bps from an early 171.
